inspectBoard.explanation: Reads an existing saved KiCad board and reports what it contains: footprints by type and side, pads, through vias, nets, holes grouped by size and plating, the Edge.Cuts outline size, minimum track width, drill and track-to-track clearance. A dependency-free host reader computes these facts and KiCad's own board statistics report (kicad-cli pcb export stats) must agree with every one of them. Outputs are board-summary.json and the native board-statistics.json. Choose it to confirm what a board file contains before checking or fabricating it; it runs no design rules.
pitfalls: Only saved two-copper-layer boards in KiCad 8.0-10.0 format are read; newer, older, multilayer or unknown formats fail with UNSUPPORTED_BOARD rather than being guessed.
Minimum track clearance follows KiCad's statistic: different-net tracks and vias compared on each item's primary layer only. It is a summary number, not a design rule check.
Mounting holes and other footprints without through_hole or smd attributes are counted as unspecified components, as KiCad does.

examples.purpose: Inspect the 30 x 20 mm fixture with four footprints and six holes.

designRuleCheck.explanation: Runs KiCad's native design rule check (kicad-cli pcb drc) on a captured copy of a saved board with every severity reported, and accepts the board only if the actual numbers of errors, warnings and unconnected items stay within the authored maximums. The board's own .kicad_pro rules and severities apply. Where the host model applies it independently predicts track/via clearance breaches and missing pad connections, which must match the native report. Outputs are board-summary.json, the native drc-report.json and board-statistics.json. Choose it before fabrication or after editing a board; exceeding a maximum fails the run with DRC_VIOLATIONS.
pitfalls: Global footprint libraries are not loaded, so library checks report lib_footprint_issues unless the project sets those checks to ignore; the summary lists every ignored check.
Zones are checked as saved: the run never refills zones, so refill and save in KiCad first if fills are stale.
Schematic parity is not checked; a board that passes here can still disagree with its schematic.

examples.purpose: Require zero errors, warnings and unconnected items on the clean fixture.

drillExport.explanation: Runs the same design rule check and, only if it passes the authored maximums, exports Excellon drill files with kicad-cli pcb export drill: decimal coordinates, absolute board origin, in millimetres or inches, with plated (PTH) and non-plated (NPTH) holes in separate files or one merged file. Every drill hit is read back independently and matched one-to-one to a board hole by position, diameter and plating. Outputs are the drill files, board-summary.json, drc-report.json and board-statistics.json. Choose it to produce the drilling data a board fabricator needs alongside layer plots from KiCad.
pitfalls: Excellon uses a y-up frame: a hole at KiCad board position (8, 10) mm is written X8.0Y-10.0.
Only round holes spanning F.Cu to B.Cu are supported; slots, drill offsets, backdrills, blind/buried vias and drilled pads on back-side footprints are rejected before KiCad runs.
No drill map, drill report or Gerber job file is produced; layer plots still come from KiCad itself.

examples.purpose: Separate PTH/NPTH millimetre drill files for the baseline fixture.
One merged inch drill file for the 40 x 25 mm variant with nine holes.

fields.explanation: A request to inspect, design-rule-check or drill-export one existing saved KiCad board. The board is referenced by path and read-only; this document only selects the operation and its acceptance limits.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis board request; it must be "schemaxis.kicad/1". It is not the KiCad release or the board file format version.

/properties/operation.explanation: What to do with the board: inspectBoard reports its contents, designRuleCheck runs KiCad's design rules against authored maximum counts, drillExport additionally writes Excellon drill files after a passing check.

/properties/operation/anyOf/0.explanation: inspectBoard: count and measure the board and confirm the counts against KiCad's statistics report.

/properties/operation/anyOf/1.explanation: designRuleCheck: run KiCad's design rules and accept the board within authored maximum counts.

/properties/operation/anyOf/2.explanation: drillExport: design-rule-check, then write and verify Excellon drill files.

/properties/board.explanation: Absolute path to an existing saved .kicad_pcb file. A sibling .kicad_pro (rules, netclasses, severities) and .kicad_dru (custom rules) with the same name are captured with it; KiCad only ever sees copies inside the run directory, so the original is never modified.
pitfalls: Relative paths are rejected; Studio and conformance resolve repository fixtures to absolute paths.
Save the board in KiCad first: autosave files and unsaved edits are not read.
Without a sibling .kicad_pro, KiCad's default rules (0.2 mm clearance) and severities apply.
/properties/board.label: Board file

/properties/maximumErrors.explanation: Largest acceptable number of DRC violations with error severity (for example clearance, shorts, minimum annular width) in the native report. The run fails with DRC_VIOLATIONS when the actual count is larger; the report and summary are kept for review. Excluded violations are reported separately and never counted.
/properties/maximumErrors.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 0, so any such finding fails the run.
pitfalls: Raising a maximum accepts findings rather than fixing them; record why in the request or review.
/properties/maximumErrors.label: Maximum errors

/properties/maximumWarnings.explanation: Largest acceptable number of DRC violations with warning severity (for example dangling tracks or silkscreen overlaps) in the native report. The run fails with DRC_VIOLATIONS when the actual count is larger; the report and summary are kept for review. Severities come from the board project; checks set to ignore are listed but not counted.
/properties/maximumWarnings.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 0, so any such finding fails the run.
pitfalls: Raising a maximum accepts findings rather than fixing them; record why in the request or review.
/properties/maximumWarnings.label: Maximum warnings

/properties/maximumUnconnected.explanation: Largest acceptable number of unconnected items (connections KiCad's ratsnest still shows as missing) in the native report. The run fails with DRC_VIOLATIONS when the actual count is larger; the report and summary are kept for review. Every routed net needs all of its pads connected by copper to reach zero.
/properties/maximumUnconnected.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 0, so any such finding fails the run.
pitfalls: Raising a maximum accepts findings rather than fixing them; record why in the request or review.
/properties/maximumUnconnected.label: Maximum unconnected items

/properties/units.explanation: Units of the coordinates and tool diameters written in the Excellon files: mm writes three decimals, in writes four. The summary and comparisons are always in millimetres.
pitfalls: Ask your fabricator which units they expect; inch files round positions to 0.0001 in (2.54 micrometres).
/properties/units.label: Drill units

/properties/separatePlating.explanation: Whether plated (board-PTH.drl) and non-plated (board-NPTH.drl) holes go in separate files. When false, one board.drl contains both, with each tool marked plated or non-plated.
/properties/separatePlating.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: true, two files; the NPTH file is written even when the board has no non-plated holes.
/properties/separatePlating.label: Separate PTH/NPTH files

/oneOf/0.explanation: Inspection request: only the board path; no design rules are run and nothing is exported.

/oneOf/1.explanation: Design rule check request: the board plus maximum error, warning and unconnected counts.

/oneOf/2.explanation: Drill export request: the design rule check fields plus drill units and the plated/non-plated file split.
